intro: Your role in mental health and dementia is to recognise, respond and report with compassion, never to diagnose, label or treat.
points: At awareness level you recognise, respond and report; diagnosis, treatment and legal decisions are for qualified professionals, not you.
Treat a sudden change in confusion or alertness as possible delirium, a medical emergency; never dismiss it as "just their dementia".
If someone talks about harming themselves or others, take it seriously and escalate straight away; never keep it to yourself.
Use respectful, person-first language and challenge stigma; see the whole person and their life history, not the diagnosis.
Treat distress reactions as signals of an unmet need — physical, emotional, environmental or communication — rather than "challenging behaviour".
Connect with the feeling behind someone's words rather than correcting facts, since people remember how you made them feel.
